outcome: Still open in general. Since 26 January 2024 there have been only partial results: a sequel that proves it for robust expanders with large maximum degree (Chen, McDonald, Shan, 2 July 2026, preprint); a Delta=4 case with a new hand proof that reports gaps in an earlier Delta=4 proof (Ge, Gutin, Qi, 12 July 2026, preprint); and two degree-condition results posted in December 2025 (Qi, Ge, Feng, 7 December 2025; Chen, Cao, 8 December 2025). Shan's 'Towards the Overfull Conjecture' (first posted August 2023, revised September 2024) is cited as published in J. Graph Theory 112(4), 2026, though I did not verify the journal record directly. No counterexample, no full resolution, and no AI-credited mathematics was found in any opened source.
problem_asks: Read from the frozen statement alone. (1) Scope: every simple graph G with maximum degree Delta(G) >= n/3, where n = |V(G)|, as the bullet words it. The sources use the strict threshold Delta > n/3; the bullet's non-strict wording is a point the judging pass must settle (see summary, where the Petersen graph minus a vertex sits exactly at Delta = n/3). (2) Direction A, the substantive one: if G is class 2 (chromatic index Delta+1), then G contains a subgraph S with Delta(S) = Delta(G) that is overfull, meaning |E(S)| > Delta(G)*floor(|V(S)|/2). (3) Direction B: if G contains an overfull subgraph S with Delta(S) = Delta(G), then G is class 2. Direction B is a counting argument (in a Delta-edge-colouring each colour class meets S in a matching of at most floor(|V(S)|/2) edges) and no source disputes it. The bullet's content is therefore Direction A. The sources also state the conjecture in Delta-critical form: every Delta-critical graph with Delta > n/3 is overfull (Qi, Ge, Feng arXiv 2512.07044 abstract). The bullet quantifies over all graphs with no restriction on Delta beyond the degree threshold, so a result restricted to a fixed Delta, a minimum degree, a density, a core condition or a large order is a case of the problem, not the problem.

I did not open the 1983 paper. Its title says order 9, so the order-10 claim rests on one secondary citation.

events.what_happened: Brinkmann and Steffen, 'Chromatic index critical graphs of orders 11 and 12', DIMACS Technical Report 97-59 (1997) and European J. Combinatorics 19 (1998), pp. 889–900. I opened the DIMACS abstract page. It states the authors determined the chromatic-index-critical graphs of orders 11 and 12 and combined this with earlier results. As summarised on that page, a critical graph is 'non-trivial' if it has at most Delta*floor(n/2) edges, i.e. is not overfull. The summary reports exactly two non-trivial critical graphs on 11 vertices, none of order 12, and exactly three non-trivial critical graphs of order at most 12. The wording 'no chromatic-index-critical graph of order 12 exists' should be read as 'no non-overfull one' given that definition; I did not open the EJC paper to confirm.

events.object: The non-overfull critical graph of order 9 is the Petersen graph with one vertex deleted, P*: 9 vertices, 12 edges, maximum degree 3 = n/3, class 2 (chromatic index 4) per the secondary sources. I re-derived by hand that P* has no subgraph S with Delta(S) = 3 and |E(S)| > 3*floor(|V(S)|/2): since P* has girth at least 5, subgraphs on 2 to 9 vertices are below the threshold in every case. The class-2 status rests on the sources and is not re-derived here. P* is explicit, not a non-constructive object. I did not confirm that Brinkmann and Steffen list P* explicitly; the sources cite them for this.

I read the arXiv HTML rendering up to its truncation point (about 140,000 of roughly 141,790 characters) and the abstract page. The main result, Theorem 1.3 as I read it, is that for every alpha > 0 and nu > 0 there are tau and n0 such that a graph G on n >= n0 vertices is class 2 exactly when it has a Delta(G)-overfull subgraph, provided that (1) Delta(G) >= alpha n and G satisfies weak VAL (d(u)+d(v) >= Delta(G)+2 for every edge uv); (2) for some small eta, fewer than eta^2 n vertices have degree deficiency above eta n; (3) G is a robust (nu, tau)-expander. The abstract states the corollary that the conjecture holds for all sufficiently large graphs with Delta >= (1+eps)n/2, for any fixed 0 < eps < 1. Authors' affiliations: Georgia State (Chen) and Auburn (McDonald, Shan).

events.remains: Graphs that are not robust expanders or violate weak VAL, graphs with Delta between n/3 and (1+eps)n/2 that fall outside those hypotheses, and all graphs below the threshold n0.

events.what_happened: Ge, Gutin and Qi, 'Edge-chromatic 4-critical graphs and Overfull Conjecture for graphs with maximum degree 4' (arXiv 2607.10947, v1 12 July 2026; v2 31 July 2026; CC BY 4.0). Abstract, as I read it from the HTML rendering: the authors prove further properties of 4-critical graphs, including four new forbidden configurations, and 'give a new structural proof of Overfull Conjecture for graphs with maximum degree 4'. Theorem 1, as I read it: for a graph G of order n with maximum degree 4 and 4 > n/3, G is class 2 (chromatic index 5) if and only if G contains an overfull subgraph H with maximum degree 4. The proof reduces necessity to a minimal 4-critical subgraph of order h in {5, 7, 9, 11} and proceeds by degree counting and Kempe-chain case analysis done by hand. The paper says Brinkmann and Steffen 'used computational methods and showed that there are exactly two non-overfull critical graphs of order 11', and that Pi (2008) has gaps, as recorded in the Pi event.
events.revisions: v1 12 July 2026; v2 31 July 2026 (current), per arXiv abstract page. The v1/v2 difference was not compared.
events.delivers: For graphs with maximum degree exactly 4 and n < 12 (from the stated hypothesis 4 > n/3), the conjecture holds: class 2 iff an overfull subgraph with Delta(H) = 4 exists. This is the Delta = 4 class, a finite check in principle for each fixed Delta, and it is restricted to that degree.
events.remains: Every maximum degree other than 4, and Delta = 4 under the bullet's non-strict threshold at n = 12 unless the order-12 result of Brinkmann and Steffen (1997) covers it.
events.time_since_posted: About 3 months at 13 October 2026, with no public engagement found in my searches
events.directly_checkable: Graphs of maximum degree 4 on at most 11 vertices are a finite family and could be checked by computer. The paper proves the case by hand. Not checked here.
events.doubts: The earlier Delta = 4 claim by Pi (2008) is reported in this paper to have gaps. This paper's argument is by hand and its correctness has not been checked by any other source I found. Authors are Ge, Gutin and Qi; Qi is also an author of arXiv 2512.07044, which this paper's condensed reference list does not cite (see that event).
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture: a full Delta = 4 case, no counterexample.

disputes.summary: Delta = 4 case: Pi (2008) claimed a proof of the overfull conjecture for Delta = 4 in 'On the overfull graph conjecture of Delta=4'. Ge, Gutin and Qi (arXiv 2607.10947, 2026) report several gaps in its main theorem and lemmas, centred on the endpoints of Kempe chains, and give a new structural proof for Delta = 4. I did not open Pi's paper to check the gaps, so the dispute is recorded as the citing paper states it.

Shan's 'Towards the Overfull Conjecture' changed between arXiv versions: v1 abstract gives eps <= 1/22 and describes an 'improvement'; v4 abstract gives eps <= 1/14 and describes a 'breakthrough'. Scope (large n, Delta >= (1-eps)n, no minimum-degree condition) is the same in both abstracts as I read them; the constant changed.

Two degree-based results on Delta-critical graphs posted one day apart in December 2025: Qi, Ge, Feng (7 Dec 2025, Delta - 5 delta/3 >= (2n-7)/3) and Chen, Cao (8 Dec 2025, Delta >= (2n+5 delta-12)/3, i.e. Delta - 5 delta/3 >= (2n-12)/3). As quoted, the Chen–Cao hypothesis is weaker, so it covers the Qi–Ge–Feng cases. This is a comparison of the two quoted conditions, not a dispute between authors.

The bullet states the threshold as Delta(G) >= n/3, but the literature (including the 2026 papers) uses Delta > n/3. Under the non-strict threshold, the Petersen graph minus a vertex (9 vertices, Delta = 3 = n/3, class 2 per the secondary sources, with no overfull subgraph that I checked by hand) would be a counterexample to Direction A. Under the strict threshold it is not. This is a point for the judging pass, not something I resolve.

Sources disagree on the year the conjecture was proposed (1985 vs 1986) and on the cited title of Chetwynd and Yap 1983 (order 9) vs its claimed scope (order at most 10). Neither affects the event dates; both are noted for the judging pass.

summary: I ran 42 web searches and opened the arXiv abstract pages and HTML renderings of every in-window preprint and most pre-window results (listed in sources). Nothing in the window settles the conjecture in full, and no counterexample was found. Five recent results give partial results: four preprints first posted in the window, and Shan's Towards I, first posted in 2023 but revised in 2024 and cited as published in 2026. (1) Chen, McDonald and Shan (arXiv 2607.02270, 2 July 2026) prove the conjecture for large robust expanders with Delta >= alpha n, weak VAL and few low-degree vertices, with a stated corollary for Delta >= (1+eps)n/2; I could read the HTML only to near its end and could not decode the PDF. (2) Ge, Gutin and Qi (arXiv 2607.10947, 12 July 2026) prove the Delta = 4 case by hand, with the hypothesis 4 > n/3 (so n <= 11), and report gaps in Pi's 2008 proof. (3) Qi, Ge and Feng (arXiv 2512.07044, 7 Dec 2025) give a sufficient degree condition, Delta - 5 delta/3 >= (2n-7)/3, for Delta-critical graphs. (4) Chen and Cao (arXiv 2512.07252, 8 Dec 2025) give Delta >= (2n+5 delta-12)/3; as quoted this is weaker than (3), so it covers all of (3)'s cases. (5) Shan's 'Towards the Overfull Conjecture' (arXiv 2308.16808, first posted 31 Aug 2023, v4 Sep 2024) proves the case Delta >= (1-eps)n for large n with no minimum-degree condition; the Ge–Gutin–Qi reference list cites it as J. Graph Theory 112(4), 2026, which I did not verify at the journal. Earlier results (events 1–21, pre-window unless noted) cover small orders (Chetwynd–Yap, Brinkmann–Steffen), Delta >= n-3 (Chetwynd–Hilton), minimum-degree and quasirandom restrictions (Plantholt, Plantholt–Shan, Shan), and critical-graph degree restrictions (Cao, Chen, Jing, Shan). Neighbouring problems are recorded as separate events and not counted as this problem: the Hilton–Zhao core and vertex-splitting conjectures (2017–2026), and the multigraph version (2023). The threshold wording is a real issue: the bullet's '>=' is contradicted at Delta = n/3 by the Petersen graph minus a vertex if that graph is class 2 (sources say it is; I verified its lack of an overfull subgraph by hand using girth 5), so the literature's strict form is what all results actually prove. AI involvement: no opened source credits an AI system with any part of the mathematics on this problem, so none_found is true for every event. Search summaries that I could not confirm claimed a ChatGPT language-editing disclosure in Towards II (2607.02270); the HTML I read contains no AI sentence but its tail was unreadable, so the claim is unverified rather than refuted. Other AI-related hits (GPT-5.6 on the Dinitz–Garg–Goemans and Petersen colouring conjectures, a ChatGPT-credited total-colouring counterexample, the Claude-related zeta and Jacobian reports, the OpenAI Erdős batches, the OpenConjecture dataset, and the Google DeepMind formal-conjectures repository) concern different problems or were not found to mention this one; I did not record them as events. Close calls: whether the Delta = 4 result (Ge–Gutin–Qi) and the Brinkmann–Steffen order-12 result together settle the bullet's Delta = 4 instance at the non-strict threshold; whether Towards I's journal status matters for weight; and whether Chen–Cao's preprint overlaps Qi–Ge–Feng's so completely that it should be read as superseding it.
competing_reading: The strongest case for a 'partial resolution' reading: the bullet's content is Direction A for all graphs with Delta >= n/3. Taken together, Shan's Towards I (Delta >= (1-eps)n, large n), the Towards II corollary (Delta >= (1+eps)n/2, large n, under robust-expansion hypotheses), Plantholt–Shan and Shan (large graphs with minimum degree near n/2) and Ge–Gutin–Qi (Delta = 4, all n) cover the top of the degree range for large n and every small order up to 12. A reader who weights these as a complete handling of large graphs with Delta >= n/2 could call the problem 'settled for large graphs with large maximum degree'. The reading against that: the gap (n/3, (1+eps)n/2) for large n is untouched, and every such result is a restricted case under extra hypotheses (robust expansion, weak VAL, minimum degree, quasirandomness or Delta-criticality). For the 'no change since 2024' reading: Towards I, although posted in 2023, was revised in 2024 and its journal publication is cited for 2026, so whether it counts as in-window depends on the revision and publication dates the judging pass adopts. A third reading treats Chen–Cao (8 Dec 2025) as superseding Qi–Ge–Feng (7 Dec 2025). The quoted inequalities make that a comparison of conditions, and nothing I read shows that either proof is wrong.
what_would_settle_it: (a) Full text of arXiv 2607.02270 (Towards II): Theorem 1.3 verbatim, its acknowledgements, and any AI-use disclosure; a PDF I can read, since the fetch tool could not decode it. (b) The J. Graph Theory 112(4) (2026) record for Towards I, to confirm acceptance, and the v1-to-v4 difference in scope and proof. (c) Pi (2008), to confirm the gaps Ge–Gutin–Qi report, and an independent check of arXiv 2607.10947's Delta = 4 proof. (d) Journal status of arXiv 2512.07044 and 2512.07252 (both unreviewed in the sources I found). (e) Whether any later paper cites arXiv 2512.07044 (the condensed reference list of 2607.10947 does not), and whether Towards II cites either December 2025 preprint. (f) A ruling on the threshold: whether the bullet means Delta >= n/3 or Delta > n/3, and whether P* is class 2 (I verified only its lack of an overfull subgraph). (g) A full-text check of Brinkmann–Steffen (EJC 1998) for the exact order-12 statement.

event.what_happened: Qi, Ge and Feng, 'A new improvement to the Overfull Conjecture' (arXiv 2512.07044, first posted 7 December 2025; single version). The abstract, as summarised from the arXiv page: every Delta-critical graph G with Delta(G) - 5 delta(G)/3 >= (2n-7)/3 is overfull, which strengthens the Cao–Chen–Jing–Shan condition Delta - 7 delta/4 >= (3n-17)/4. The search snippet and the page-level summary both give the inequality as Delta(G) - 5delta(G)/3 >= (2n-7)/3. No journal reference is listed; the authors are from Hebei University of Science and Technology.
event.revisions: v1 7 Dec 2025 only (per arXiv abstract page).
event.delivers: For Delta-critical graphs satisfying Delta - 5 delta/3 >= (2n-7)/3: the graph is overfull. Restricted to the degree inequality, and to Delta-critical graphs.
event.remains: Delta-critical graphs outside the inequality, in particular those with minimum degree near Delta/2 or below, and all non-critical graphs (which the Delta-critical reduction covers in principle).

event.doubts: The degree condition in this preprint (Delta - 5 delta/3 >= (2n-7)/3) is a stronger requirement than the one in the Chen–Cao preprint of 8 December 2025 (Delta >= (2n+5 delta-12)/3, i.e. Delta - 5 delta/3 >= (2n-12)/3). Every graph satisfying the Qi–Ge–Feng condition satisfies the Chen–Cao condition, so the two results overlap and the later preprint covers more. This is arithmetic from the two abstracts as quoted and is not a claim about correctness. The paper was not reviewed in the sources I found and I did not read its full text.

judgement.why: Every result in the record proves the conjecture under extra hypotheses (degree range, minimum degree, criticality plus degree inequality, quasirandomness, robust expansion, fixed Delta), so each is a case; none settles the full statement. Small-order computer classifications (Chetwynd–Yap, Brinkmann–Steffen) are finite checks, so instances. Hilton–Zhao core/vertex-splitting and multigraph results are different questions, so variant. Shan's Towards I keeps its August 2023 date: the 2024 v4 only improved the constant within the same scope, so it is not a new event. Pi 2008 is knocked down by the specific Kempe-chain gaps Ge–Gutin–Qi report. Post-snapshot preprints are unreviewed but by established researchers with no identified error. No event credits any AI system.
judgement.doubts: Ge–Gutin–Qi's Delta=4 result covers only n<=11, a finite family; it was scored case (a hand proof of a named restriction) though instances is arguable. The statement's non-strict threshold Delta>=n/3 would make the classical Petersen-minus-a-vertex graph a counterexample; the literature uses the strict form, and this pre-snapshot, classical observation was not scored as a refutation. The possible ChatGPT language-editing disclosure in Towards II is unverified; even if real it would be prose, i.e. none.
